reason: E2 directly supports that interstitial N increases SFE in a medium-entropy alloy, but the cited evidence does not address the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system, its caloric phase transformation, or the claimed fracture toughness improvement. E1 is about a different alloy and mechanism (hydrogen embrittlement) and provides no support for the key premises.
premises: Interstitial nitrogen increases stacking fault energy (SFE) in FCC high-entropy/medium-entropy alloys
Increased SFE suppresses deformation twinning and crack initiation, improving fracture toughness
A small nitrogen addition (~0.4 at.%) will not significantly impair the reversible phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect
The effect of nitrogen on SFE observed in CoCrNi can be extrapolated to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy system
